s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory distress with bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to broad-spectrum antibiotics, occurring in the context of recent immunotherapy
salient_findings: New bilateral infiltrative shadows on chest CT
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
No clinical improvement with antibiotics or high-dose corticosteroids
key_facts: 82-year-old man
Recent treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab
Follow-up chest CT showed new bilateral infiltrative shadows
Patient reported fever and dyspnea
Elevated C-reactive protein and surfactant protein D levels
Krebs von den Lungen-6 was normal
Sputum cultures, procalcitonin, and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative
Serologic testing for various autoantibodies was negative
No history of antigen exposure
No clinical improvement with lascufloxacin or tazobactam/ceftolozane
Oxygen requirement increased to 2 L/min and later to 4 L/min
No clinical improvement with high-dose corticosteroids
Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid contained 29% neutrophils, 58% lymphocytes, 13% macrophages
CD4/CD8 ratio of 0.33
Transbronchial lung biopsy showed no malignancy

shortlist.label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab, consistent with clinical presentation of pneumonitis

shortlist.label: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to broad-spectrum antibiotics, possible reaction to environmental or drug exposure

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Immunocompromised state due to recent immunotherapy, opportunistic infection possible

shortlist.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral infiltrative shadows and lack of response to broad-spectrum antibiotics, possible idiopathic condition

shortlist.label: Acute interstitial pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid onset of respiratory symptoms and bilateral infiltrative shadows, consistent with acute interstitial pneumonia

raw.rationale: The patient's recent treatment with ipilimumab and nivolumab, followed by the development of new bilateral infiltrative shadows, fever, and dyspnea, is consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis. The lack of response to antibiotics and the presence of lymphocytosis in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid further support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: Sputum cultures and SARS-CoV-2 PCR were negative, and the patient's symptoms and lab results do not suggest an opportunistic infection

rejected.label: Cryptogenic organizing pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis, and the lack of response to corticosteroids is not typical of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia

rejected.label: Acute interstitial pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with ICI-induced pneumonitis, and the presence of lymphocytosis in the bronchoalveolar lavage fluid supports an immune-mediated process
